newsitem.title: UK: MTL confirmed winner of northeast rail franchise.
newsitem.headline: MTL confirmed winner of northeast rail franchise.

text.p: UK transport group MTL Rail Ltd has been awarded the passenger rail franchise for Regional Railways North East and said on Monday it was committed to investing in rolling stock and spending 500,000 stg a year on station improvements.

MTL, which also runs bus operations in northeast England and London, was given the franchise for a seven and a half year term, said the Office of Passenger Rail Franchising in a statement. Its subsidy for the first year will be 224.5 million stg, falling to 145.6 million in the financial year 2003/04.

The group was announced as preferred bidder at the end of January. Its winning bid commits the group to operate at least the same number of train miles for the term and introduce 16 new three-car electric multiple carriage units by 2000, replacing older models.
It has pledged to raise punctuality standards by one percentage point to 91 percent from March 1999, raising it further to 92 percent by 2001.
The franchise covers rail services in the Scottish border region plus parts of northern England, including Manchester, Liverpool, Sheffield and Leeds.
Passenger revenue for the franchise for the year ended March 31 was 68 million stg. As of September last year it employed 2,960 staff.
The announcement moves the UK government closer to completion of the sale of the 25 franchises.
There are only two franchises left to be appointed a preferred bidder -- Central Trains and ScotRail.
